newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IMPLATS SAYS WAGE STRIKE OVER.
newsitem.headline: IMPLATS SAYS WAGE STRIKE OVER.

text.p: South Africa's Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd said on Monday a deal had been struck with more than 400 striking workers at its platinum refineries, and that full production would resume on Tuesday morning.
"They reached a negotiated settlement very late this afternoon," Implats refineries spokeswoman Marilyn Watson told Reuters.
"We are going to put something out tomorrow morning (Tuesday) on the figures -- Apparently it's a win-win situation."
Watson said the operations were expected to return to normal early on Tuesday, adding: "They are expected to report for work tomorrow morning."
The strikers, all members of the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM), embarked on the industrial action over wages on August 4.
Watson said earlier on Monday that production had not been affected because non-striking members of the 1,100-strong workforce had kept the refineries going.
Management's last wage offer was a 10.7 percent increase, against the NUM's last demand of 19.2 percent. It is unclear what the current settlement entails.
Implats produced 499,000 ounces of refined platinum in the six months to end-December 1996 and normal output is around a million ounces a year.
